description: Juniper EX2500-24F, a fixed 1RU 10 GbE top-of-rack switch with 24 SFP+ ports. The front carries the 24 ports in six gangs of four, four system lamps, two management jacks, a mini-USB serial console and a reset button. The rear carries two AC power inlets beside a vented panel. The two supplies and six fans are built in, so there are no bays. One panel serves both models: the -FB moves air front to back and the -BF back to front.

gaps.wanted: The dimensions and positions of the two-post and four-post kits. Tables 16 and 17 and Figures 4 to 9 list and draw the parts, and the panel figures show no ear.
A straight-on studio photograph of each side. The only photograph is the datasheet's cover picture, a perspective view of the front right corner, so every position is read from the figures.
The part numbers and faces of the two internal supplies and the six fans. The guide names them by role only and says they are built in.
The part number of the mini-USB to D9 console cable. The guide gives its wiring in Table 7 and no code.
What the ST-A lamp shows. Table 8 calls it a status LED and gives no states.
The position of the two management jacks' own lamps. The figure draws small squares at the jack corners, and the photograph shows a green one at the lower left of jack A.

The hardware of the protective earthing terminal and its size. The earth symbol is placed from Figure 2, which draws no lug, stud or screw at it. The guide's safety text names the terminal without describing it.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.

furniture.description: the two screws on the rear panel and the earth symbol at its left end

mgmt.mixed: the management cluster at the right of the front: two RJ-45 management ports, A and B, and a mini-USB serial console. Two kinds, one purpose: reaching the switch when the data ports cannot.

power-input.description: The two IEC 320 inlets, one for each internal supply

sfp-plus.description: The 24 SFP+ ports as printed, 1 to 24, each taking a 10 GbE SFP+ or direct access cable, or a 1 GbE optic

sfp-plus-activity-leds.description: The L/A lamp of each SFP+ port, the left of the pair over the cage (Table 10)

sfp-plus-speed-leds.description: The SP lamp of each SFP+ port, the right of the pair over the cage; lit at 10 Gbps, off at 1 Gbps (Table 10)

status-leds.description: The four system lamps SYS, FAN, ST-A and ST-B (Table 8)

name: ex2500-24f

airflow.note: Table 12 and the datasheet: the EX2500-24F-FB moves air front to back and the EX2500-24F-BF back to front; the datasheet's Figure 1 draws both. One panel serves both, so each model is a configuration.

chassis.note: Table 12: 4.4 x 43.9 x 38.1 cm (1.73 x 17.3 x 15.0 in), 6.4 kg (14.1 lb), the same for the -FB and the -BF. THE DATASHEET DISAGREES on the weight: it gives 14.9 lb (6.8 kg), and 1.7 x 17.3 x 15 in. The guide's figures are used because Table 12 gives them per model; the datasheet's weight is kept in attrs. 1RU. The width is the body: the drawings show no mounting brackets.

chassis-lamps.note: Figure 3 and Table 8: four round lamps in a column at the left, SYS, FAN, ST-A and ST-B, 10.4 mm from the left edge and 16.8, 21.9, 26.9 and 32.1 mm down. Table 9: SYS is solid green with both supplies good and blinking green with one failed or one cord connected; FAN is solid green with the fans good and blinking with a failure. ST-A is a status lamp whose meaning the guide does not give, and ST-B is reserved for future use.

colour.note: The figures are line drawings. The body is a near black read from the datasheet's cover photograph, a perspective view of the front right corner, with silver cages and white printing. A photograph that is not in perspective would settle the shade.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. Tables 16 and 17 and Figures 4 to 9 describe a standard two-post kit and a four-post kit, and Table 15 and the datasheet order the generic four-post kit as EX2500-RMK-4POST. The drawings of the panels show no ear, so no ear position is stated, and no kit is listed in chassis.kits.

environment.note: Table 13: operating 0 to +40 C, 0 to +35 C with a fan or supply failed, storage -20 to +70 C, 10 to 90 percent humidity operating, altitude 3,050 m operating, under 65 dB. THE DATASHEET DISAGREES on the operating minimum: it gives -10 C (14 F). The guide's range is used.

fans.note: Guide, Fans: six internal fans, and fans are not customer replaceable. The datasheet says redundant, variable-speed. They are not field-replaceable units, so there is no bay, and the guide gives no part number or face for them.

gate-1.note: Figures 1 and 2 are vector line drawings and were rendered at 600 dpi and measured with a pixel ruler. The front figure's body is 3607 px across and 295 px down: 0.1217 mm per px across from the 439 mm of Table 12 and 0.1492 down from its 44.0 mm. The drawing is not at one scale, 22 percent tighter down than across, and the check is the cage opening: it reads 10.4 mm down on that scale, the registry's 10.4, on a quantity the scale never saw. The rear figure is 3622 px across and 341 px down: 0.1212 across and 0.1287 down, a 7 percent aspect error. Every position read off a figure is estimated, to about a millimetre across and 1.5 mm down. The mirror's raster is the figure as printed, so a dimension it could not give was not read from it.

lifecycle.note: The product is end of life and Juniper no longer hosts its documents. No end-of-life notice is held, so no lifecycle is written.

management.note: Figure 1: two RJ-45 jacks stacked in one frame at the right, B above A, 424.1 mm across and 14.8 and 29.0 mm down, with their letters at 436 mm. Table 11 gives their lamps: link (solid green with a link, blinking with activity) and speed (solid green at 100 or 1000 Mbps, off at 10). Below them are the mini-USB console CON, centred at 396 mm and 33.2 mm down, and the RESET button, centred at 408.9 mm and 32.9 mm down. The guide: "1 RS-232 console port (mini-USB)", and an external cable converts it to D9. The datasheet's list says "RS-232 DB9 console port", which the guide corrects for the unit.

ordering-codes.note: Table 15 prints EX2500-24F-FB and EX2500-24F-BF. The datasheet's ordering table prints the first as EX2500-2F-FB, which is read as a misprint of the guide's code.

port-lamps.note: Figure 1 and Figure 3: two round lamps over each cage, centred on it and 6.1 mm apart, 20.7 mm down. The leader lines of Figure 3 put L/A on the left lamp and SP on the right. Table 10: L/A is solid green with a link and no activity, blinking green with activity, and off with no link; SP is solid green at 10 Gbps and off at 1 Gbps.

ports.note: Figure 1: 24 SFP+ ports in one row, printed 1 to 24, in six gangs of four. The cage frames start 62.8 mm apart from 16.9 mm in; within a gang the frames are 14.76 mm apart, 3.6 percent over the registry's 14.25 mm pitch, so the drawn pitch is used with the gutter between gangs at 62.8 - 4 x 14.76 = 3.76 mm. The cage opening is 10.4 mm high and its top is 25.6 mm down. The numerals stand under each cage, their centres 40.1 mm down. The guide says the ports take approved SFP+ transceivers and direct access cables, and the datasheet says each runs at 1 GbE or 10 GbE.

power.note: Table 14: two supplies, 1+1 redundant, 275 W each, 100 to 240 VAC universal, 50 to 60 Hz, 2.75 A at 100 VAC and 1.15 A at 240 VAC, system dissipation 200 W typical. The datasheet gives 192 W average at full line rate. Table 13: 1100 BTU an hour maximum.

rear-earth.note: Figure 2 (page 4), read at 600 dpi on the rear figure's pixel ruler (0.1212 mm per px across, 0.1287 down): a circled earth symbol on the bare panel at the left of the left inlet, centred 6.5 mm from the left edge and 2.8 mm below the inlet's centre (23.3 mm down). It is about 8.6 mm across in the figure while the registered symbol is 6.0 mm, so it is centred on the figure's mark and is smaller. The figure draws no plate, lug, stud or screw, and no page names a lug, a screw size or a thread, so nothing is drawn for the terminal. Six small plain circles, three at each end, are not placed. Reading accuracy about 1 mm across and 1.5 mm down.

rear-layout.note: Figure 2: an inlet at each end, centred 24.0 and 414.9 mm across and 20.5 mm down, each drawn portrait, 22 mm across by 35 mm high with its three pins stacked, so it is the library's C14 inlet turned a quarter. Guide, Power Supplies: two internal 275 W supplies, each with its own IEC 320 inlet on the rear and no power switch. The supplies are internal and the guide gives no part number for them.

sources.note: EX2500 Ethernet Switch Hardware Guide (Juniper Networks, 61 pages), read via mirror: the copy held is a ManualsLib reproduction of Juniper's manual, the only copy found, since Juniper no longer hosts it. Used: Figures 1 and 2 (the front and rear panels), Figure 3 (the lamps), Tables 4 to 11 (ports, console and lamps), Table 12 (envelope and weight), Table 13 (environment), Table 14 (power) and Table 15 (part numbers). EX2500 Ethernet Switches datasheet (Juniper Networks, 1000282-001-EN, Apr 2009, 4 pages): the cover photograph, the specifications and the ordering information. No studio photograph, stencil or 3D model of the EX2500 is held. Terms: both documents are Juniper's and are read for facts only; nothing of either is copied into the library.

vents.note: Figure 1: a hexagonal vent field over the whole width of the face from 1.9 to 17.5 mm down, a smaller one at the right of port 24 above the console, and in the figure the lamps and the maker's logo sit in it at the left. Figure 2: a vented panel between the two inlets, 51.5 to 386.7 mm across, its hexagon field from 67.6 to 370.6 mm, with two cross-head screws at its right end. The panel is where the six fans exhaust or draw in. The fans themselves are not drawn: no figure shows a fan face.
